prompt: What is the greatest solution to $2x^2 - 8x = 0$?
hint: Factor out the greatest common factor first.

hints.text: Factor out the greatest common factor first.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a smaller one: $x^2 - 3x = 0$ factors to $x(x - 3) = 0$, so $x = 0$ or $x = 3$. Pull out the common factor and read both roots — never divide the $x$ away.

learningObjective: Solve a quadratic by factoring out a common monomial.
explanation: Set the product to zero: $2x = 0$ gives $x = 0$, and $x - 4 = 0$ gives $x = 4$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Pull out the constant first if it helps
steps: You could also factor as $2(x^2 - 4x) = 2 \cdot x(x - 4)$.
The constant $2$ can never be zero, so it contributes no solution — only the variable factors matter.
Recognizing that a numerical factor is irrelevant to the roots saves you from chasing it.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Dividing both sides by x turns 2x² = 8x into 2x = 8 — the root x = 0 vanishes without a trace.
Factor a zero product instead of dividing: 2x(x − 4) = 0 keeps both roots, and then greatest-vs-least is a safe final read.
